1.explanation:
All of the mis‐highlighting stems from the cshtml grammar defined in prism-cshtml.js.  
1. The helper directive (@helper) isn’t included in the ‘block’ pattern, so Prism never recognizes or styles it as a Razor block.  
2. The ‘value’ pattern, responsible for matching @expressions inside text and attribute contexts, doesn’t fully account for namespaced method calls with nested parentheses and quotes (e.g. @Localize.GetLabelHtml("…")).  
3. The nested() helper function builds the bracket patterns (round, square, angle, curly) used by both ‘block’ and ‘value’; any deficiency here propagates into all patterns relying on it.  
To fix the issue, you must update the ‘block’ definition to include a case for @helper, enhance the ‘value’ regex to handle dot-qualified method calls with nested string literals, and/or refine nested() so it correctly respects quoted strings and embedded parentheses in attribute expressions.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting Razor (.cshtml) code with Prism, certain C# constructs inside HTML attributes and helper directives are not recognized correctly. In the screenshots, the placeholder attribute value “@Localize.GetLabelHtml("PLACEHOLDER")” is treated as plain markup/string instead of C# code, and the “@helper TrialHelper(string name){…}” block isn’t tokenized as a Razor block at all.

2.explanation: All of the incorrect highlighting stems from the cshtml language definition in components/prism-cshtml.js. The ‘nested’ helper builds bracket patterns but explicitly omits HTML expressions, so expressions inside attributes (e.g. placeholder="@Localize…") are never passed to the C# highlighter. The ‘block’ token covers @{…} and control‐flow constructs but does not include @helper, so helper blocks are not recognized as Razor code. The ‘directive’ pattern lists only a fixed set of @keywords (addTagHelper, inject, section, etc.) and omits @helper. Finally the ‘value’ pattern is only applied at the top level (not inside HTML attributes) and thus misses calls like @Localize.GetLabelHtml(…) in tag contexts. All of these patterns live in the Prism.languages.insertBefore('cshtml','prolog',…) call that defines razor-comment, block, directive, value and delegate-operator tokens. To fix the bug you must adjust the tagRegion/html grammar to pass attribute values through the C# highlighter and extend the block/directive patterns to recognize @helper.
2.bug_scenario: When Prism highlights .cshtml (Razor) files it mis-colors valid Razor constructs such as the @helper directive and interpolated expressions inside HTML attributes (e.g. placeholder="@Localize.GetLabelHtml(…)" ). In the screenshots you can see that P rism treats those @… calls as plain markup or text, whereas Visual Studio highlights them as C# code. The gist of the problem is that the cshtml language definition in Prism (components/prism-cshtml.js) does not recognize @helper blocks and does not apply the C# “value” pattern inside tag attributes.
